summary: Creating your own Slack OAuth app is quick and needs no review if you keep it unlisted: create the app at api.slack.com/apps, add Composio's callback as a redirect URL, pick scopes, turn on public distribution, and paste the client ID and secret into a Composio custom auth config. The catch is commercial use. Since May 29, 2025, Slack's API terms say the Slack Marketplace is the only appropriate channel for commercially distributing an app, and new installs of unlisted commercial apps are limited to 1 request per minute (15 objects per request) on conversations.history and conversations.replies. If your agent needs to read message history for paying customers, plan for a Marketplace listing, which needs 10 active workspaces first and then up to 10 business days of preliminary review plus up to 10 weeks of functional review. Until then you can keep using Composio's managed Slack app.

difficulty.reason: Setup is self-serve and takes under an hour with no review for an unlisted app. It becomes Hard if your product is commercial and reads message history, because the unlisted rate limit makes history reading close to unusable and the Marketplace route needs 10 active workspaces and a review of up to about 12 weeks.

evidence.label: INFERRED
evidence.note: Level is our judgement, based on the official distribution guide, the May 2025 rate limit changelog and the Marketplace review guide.

time.detail: Hands-on: 30-90 min to create the app, set scopes and redirect URL, and wire up Composio. Preparing a Marketplace submission (video, test accounts, scope reasons) is extra work, likely a few days.. Approval wait: Unlisted app: no wait. Marketplace listing: up to 10 business days for preliminary review plus up to 10 weeks for functional review (6 weeks for resubmissions of published apps), and only after you reach 10 active workspaces.

evidence.label: INFERRED
evidence.note: Review durations are stated by Slack (SOURCED, s5) as upper bounds. The 0-84 day range is ours: 0 for the unlisted path most builders start on, up to about 14 calendar days plus 70 days for a commercial app that must be listed. Hands-on minutes are estimated from the number of settings pages, not stated by Slack. Time to reach 10 active workspaces is not included.

requirements.name: Slack account and a development workspace
requirements.detail: You create the app while signed in to Slack and pick a development workspace. You can still distribute it to other workspaces later.

requirements.name: HTTPS redirect URL
requirements.detail: The redirect_uri must use HTTPS. Composio's callback https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback meets this.

requirements.name: Public distribution turned on
requirements.detail: Without it the app installs only in its own workspace. Activate Public Distribution under Manage Distribution after completing the checklist. No review is involved.

requirements.name: Slack Marketplace listing
requirements.detail: Needed if you distribute commercially, by Slack's API terms, and in practice if you read channel history at scale. Requires at least 10 active workspaces (used in the past 28 days), a video of install and OAuth, test accounts with dummy data and reasons for each scope.

requirements.name: Composio custom auth config
requirements.detail: Only needed if you want your own app instead of Composio's managed Slack app (branding, custom scopes, own rate limits).

scopes.name: chat:write
scopes.purpose: Bot scope to post messages as the app.

evidence.label: INFERRED
evidence.note: No scope triggers review for an unlisted app. In a Marketplace submission every requested scope is reviewed and must be justified.

scopes.name: channels:read
scopes.purpose: Bot scope to list public channels so the agent can find where to act.

evidence.label: INFERRED
evidence.note: Common choice for agents; sensitivity rating is ours.

scopes.name: users:read
scopes.purpose: Bot scope to look up people in the workspace.

scopes.name: channels:history
scopes.purpose: Bot scope to read messages in public channels via conversations.history and conversations.replies.

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: Does not trigger a review on its own, but new installs of unlisted commercial apps are limited to 1 request per minute and 15 objects on the history methods. Slack calls bulk reading a data exfiltration risk.

scopes.name: groups:history, im:history
scopes.purpose: Bot scopes to read private channels and direct messages the app is in.

evidence.label: INFERRED
evidence.note: Same history methods and rate limit as channels:history. We rate these sensitive; Slack does not label scopes this way in the pages we read.

scopes.name: search:read
scopes.purpose: User scope (user_scope) to search messages on behalf of the person who connects.

evidence.label: INFERRED
evidence.note: Slack's guide uses search:read as its example user scope. Sensitivity rating is ours.

steps.title: Create the Slack app
steps.action: Sign in at api.slack.com/apps, click Create New App, enter a name and choose a development workspace.
steps.expected_result: The app's settings page opens, with Basic Information and OAuth & Permissions in the sidebar.

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: Our probe only confirmed the console page loads (HTTP 200); the steps come from Slack's docs.

steps.title: Add Composio's redirect URL
steps.action: In OAuth & Permissions, under Redirect URLs, add https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback and save. Use the same value in the Composio auth config.
steps.expected_result: The redirect URL is listed. A redirect_uri sent later must match it or be a subdirectory of it.

steps.title: Choose bot and user scopes
steps.action: Write down the smallest set of scopes your agent needs (bot scopes and any user scopes), then add them under OAuth & Permissions > Scopes. Do not add scopes for features you have not built yet.
steps.expected_result: Scopes appear in the list. An agent can draft the list and a reason for each; a signed-in person enters them.

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: Slack advises requesting only what you need because workspace admins judge apps by their scopes.

steps.title: Leave PKCE off and decide on token rotation
steps.action: Do not enable PKCE for a Composio app, and only enable token rotation if you are sure your stack refreshes tokens. Both settings cannot be turned off afterwards.
steps.expected_result: The app stays a confidential client that uses its client secret, with tokens that do not expire.

evidence.label: INFERRED
evidence.note: Slack says PKCE makes the app a public client that does not send client_secret and can only be undone via Slack support, and token rotation cannot be turned off. Composio's setup asks for a client ID and secret, so we infer PKCE should stay off. Whether Composio handles Slack rotating tokens for custom apps is unverified.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.action: Open Manage Distribution, complete the checklist under Share Your App with Other Workspaces, and click Activate Public Distribution.
steps.expected_result: Other workspaces can install the app through OAuth. No review is needed for this unlisted state.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret
steps.action: Open Basic Information > App Credentials and copy the Client ID and Client Secret. Store the secret in a secret manager, not in code.
steps.expected_result: You have both values ready for Composio.

steps.title: Create a custom auth config in Composio
steps.action: In the Composio dashboard click Create Auth Config, pick Slack, choose OAuth2, turn on Use your own developer credentials, paste the client ID and secret, set the Redirect URI to the Composio callback and add your scopes. Copy the auth config ID.
steps.expected_result: An auth config ID such as ac_... is shown.

steps.title: Use the config and test an install
steps.action: Pass the auth config ID in your session's auth_configs for slack, then connect a test user from a second workspace and run one read and one write action.
steps.expected_result: The consent screen shows your app name, and the connected account works in the second workspace.

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: Toolkits not listed in auth_configs keep using Composio's managed app.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace if you sell the product
steps.action: Once the app is active in at least 10 workspaces, submit it for listing with a video of install and OAuth, test accounts with dummy data, install access for reviewers and a reason for every scope.
steps.expected_result: Preliminary feedback within up to 10 business days, then a functional review of up to 10 weeks.

review_process.trigger: No review for an unlisted distributed app. A Slack Marketplace review is needed to list the app, and Slack's API terms (updated May 29, 2025) say the Marketplace is the only appropriate channel for commercial distribution.
what_to_submit: Proof of at least 10 active workspaces (used in the past 28 days)
Video of the full install, OAuth flow and set-up
Test account credentials for your service, with dummy data
A way for reviewers to install the app (they cannot access any Slack workspace)
A reason for each requested scope
For later updates: a test or staging app identical to the published one
review_process.typical_wait: Up to 10 business days for preliminary review, then up to 10 weeks for functional review (6 weeks for published apps resubmitting). Queue position resets on each resubmission during preliminary review.
common_rejections: App not production-ready, in private beta or still being built
Scopes requested for features planned for the future
Legacy, restricted or coded workflow scopes
Not meeting the Marketplace guidelines in full

blockers.blocker: Unlisted commercial apps get 1 request per minute and at most 15 objects on conversations.history and conversations.replies for new installs.
blockers.how_to_get_past: Get listed in the Slack Marketplace, or design the agent around the Events API and targeted reads instead of bulk history. Internal customer-built apps are not affected.

blockers.blocker: The Marketplace requires at least 10 active workspaces before you can submit.
blockers.how_to_get_past: Run a pilot as an unlisted app (or on Composio's managed app) with early customers until you reach 10 active workspaces.

blockers.blocker: Some workspaces only let admins install apps, require admin approval, or allow only Marketplace apps.
blockers.how_to_get_past: Ask the customer's workspace admin to approve the install. Keep scopes minimal, since admins judge by them. For Marketplace-only workspaces you need a listing.

agent_did: Fetched Slack's OpenID discovery document (it exists, but it serves Sign in with Slack only and lists no PKCE methods).
Called the OAuth v2 authorize endpoint with a fake client ID; the result was inconclusive because the page is rendered by JavaScript.
Checked that the app console at api.slack.com/apps loads.
Checked that the Installing with OAuth guide loads.
agent_can: Draft the minimal scope list and a reason for each scope
Write Marketplace listing text and test instructions
Check Slack docs and changelog for rate limit or terms changes
Test a connected account once a person has finished OAuth
human_must: Sign in to Slack and create the app
Enter the redirect URL and scopes, and activate public distribution
Copy the client secret and store it safely
Sign in to Composio and create the custom auth config
Accept Slack's API terms and submit the Marketplace review, including recording the video
Ask customer workspace admins to approve installs where needed

nuances.detail: Slack OAuth tokens do not expire by default. They are revoked if the app is uninstalled, the user removes it, or the installing user is deactivated. Apps using scopes beyond bot, incoming-webhook, commands and identify are uninstalled automatically if the installing user leaves the workspace or becomes a guest.

With token rotation on, access tokens expire every 12 hours (expires_in 43200) and each refresh token is used once. Rotation cannot be turned off once on. With PKCE enabled, refresh tokens expire after 30 days.

Slack supports PKCE with S256 only. Turning it on makes the app a public client, the code exchange omits client_secret, and only Slack support can turn it off. Slack's docs page does not give the date PKCE was added. For a Composio app that uses a client secret, leave it off.

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: Advice to leave it off is our inference from Composio asking for a client secret.

nuances.detail: Slack's OpenID discovery document exists but describes Sign in with Slack (openid.connect endpoints), not the oauth/v2 install flow, and it lists no PKCE methods. Do not use it to configure the install flow.

redirect_uri must use HTTPS and must match, or be a subdirectory of, a Redirect URL configured on the app. If several are configured, send the same redirect_uri in both the authorize and access steps or you get bad_redirect_uri.

From May 29, 2025, conversations.history and conversations.replies drop from Tier 3 to Tier 1 (1 request per minute, 15 objects) for new installs of commercially distributed non-Marketplace apps. Existing installs of such apps, Marketplace apps and internal customer-built apps are not affected.
Scopes are additive: re-running OAuth adds new scopes to the token and you cannot remove scopes without revoking it. Adding scopes later means existing workspaces must reinstall.

Each workspace install gets its own tokens. Passing an Enterprise organization ID in the team parameter asks for an org-level install, which may need an Org Owner or Admin. Slack recommends checking that the connecting user's domain matches the customer's workspace.

unverified: The date Slack added PKCE support; the PKCE page and changelog we checked do not give one.
Whether Composio's custom auth config refreshes Slack rotating tokens (token rotation on) correctly.
Which scopes Composio's managed Slack app requests by default.
The authorize endpoint check was inconclusive, so we have no automated proof of how Slack rejects a bad client ID.
Whether the Marketplace review guide requires a privacy policy; the page we read did not say.

composio_note.detail: Composio lists Slack among its managed OAuth apps, so you can start on Composio's app today with no Slack setup. Switch to your own app when you need your own name on the consent screen, scopes beyond Composio's defaults, a dedicated rate limit instead of shared quota, or polling triggers faster than the 15-minute minimum of managed auth. Note that Slack's Marketplace and rate limit rules apply to whichever app your users install.
